name: bt10-ios-player
title: Build targets stage 10: iOS and macOS players with the software renderer, built and simulator-tested in GitHub Actions, started from the editor
issue: User request, 2026-11-10: 'I would like for the engine to be able to allow the user to select a build target in the engine editor UI like windows, linux, android, ios, web, and maybe other console toolchains in the future like switch'. Design and stage table: orchestrator/proposals/build-targets-design.md. Stage 10 of section 5.
acceptance: A GitHub Actions workflow on a macOS runner builds the ios target (simulator build) and the macos target, runs a Lua 2D sample on the iOS simulator and the macOS player headless, and uploads both as artifacts

The editor's Build for an Apple target starts the workflow with gh, follows it and downloads the artifact; n2build doctor checks gh and its login instead of Xcode (a small frontend item if the panel needs changes)
Touch, gamepad, lifecycle, safe area, audio session and saves are implemented and covered by simulator tests where the simulator allows; a device checklist exists for when a device is available
Device signing only through repository secrets used inside the workflow, never in the project, logs or protocol; unsigned simulator builds work without them
The ios and macos targets' physics as for android (decision D8)
gate: needs the user's go; depends on bt4-vfs-packs and bt7-renderer-surfaces; D8 decided: Jolt and Box2D only. D2: software renderer here, Metal in bt13-metal-renderer. D5: macOS included. D7: no Mac, GitHub Actions only
notes: Reviewer: no private API, App Store rules on code loading respected (Lua interpreted, no JIT), secrets only in the workflow, the workflow pinned (runner image, Xcode version).
